headline: Double-digit growth across sales, backlog, and earnings
summary_short: Elbit Systems reported Q2 2026 revenue of $2,287.1 million, up 16.0% y/y, with GAAP diluted EPS of $3.61 (+34.2% y/y) and a record order backlog of $32.0 billion.
summary_long: Revenue rose 16.0% y/y to $2,287.1M, led by Land (+32%, ammunition/munitions in Israel), ISTAR and EW (+22%, laser/EW/maritime systems in Asia-Pacific), and Elbit Systems of America (+17%, favorable project mix and night-vision/maritime sales); Aerospace fell 8% on an unfavorable project mix and lower European training/simulation sales. GAAP operating income rose 38.7% to $218.8M and net income rose 38.1% to $173.6M, in line with the increase in activity; financial expenses fell to $22.0M from $31.2M on lower average debt. Order backlog reached a record $32.0B, driven mainly by Europe, with 73% attributable to orders outside Israel. The board declared a $1.00/share dividend, and six-month operating cash flow rose to $517.8M from $304.0M.
confidence_notes: No formal forward-looking financial guidance (revenue/EPS ranges) was given in this release, so nothing was written to the guidance array. The higher effective tax rate (16.4% vs 5.6% y/y) was attributed by the company to implementation of OECD Pillar II global minimum tax rules, not an operating factor.

drivers.explanation: Growth was led by Land (+32%, ammunition and munitions sales in Israel), ISTAR and EW (+22%, laser/EW/maritime systems in Asia-Pacific), and Elbit Systems of America (+17%, favorable project mix, night-vision and maritime sales).
The increase in net income was in line with the increase in the Company's business activity; financial expenses also fell on lower average debt.
The increase in backlog during the quarter came mainly from Europe; approximately 73% of the current backlog is attributable to orders outside Israel.

Management cited double-digit growth in sales, backlog, and EPS, improved profitability, strong cash flow generation, and continued investment in production capacity and new laser/directed-energy capabilities.
